ei.subject: 수능특강Light 영어
ei.title: 미디어를 통한 고정관념의 형성과 자기실현적 예언

fullPassage: We learn many stereotypes from the media, rather than our personal experiences. Media offerings repeatedly present viewers with depictions of persons from all races and ethnicities, people living in poverty and older adults that leave impressions of what they are like. Too often, these depictions devalue and reduce members belonging to these groups to a simple and single concept. Then, when we interact with persons from these social categories, stereotypes are triggered without our even being aware of it. These stereotypes generate in us an expectation of how a member of the group will behave. When we then act on those expectations, we precipitate a self-fulfilling prophecy. We see the behavior that confirms our expectation whether or not it is actually present. Thus, if we assume that someone is rude to us, they will appear rude, even when they act benevolently.

questions.passage: We learn many stereotypes from the media, rather than our personal experiences. Media offerings repeatedly present viewers with depictions of persons from all races and ethnicities, people living in poverty and older adults that leave impressions of what they are like. Too often, these depictions (A)[devalue / elevate] and reduce members belonging to these groups to a simple and single concept. Then, when we interact with persons from these social categories, stereotypes are triggered without our even being aware of it. These stereotypes generate in us an expectation of how a member of the group will behave. When we then act on those expectations, we precipitate a self-fulfilling prophecy. We see the behavior that (B)[confirms / denies] our expectation whether or not it is actually present. Thus, if we assume that someone is rude to us, they will appear rude, even when they act (C)[benevolently / maliciously].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ devalue — confirms — benevolently: 묘사가 구성원을 '평가절하'하고, 기대를 '확인'하는 행동을 보며, 상대가 '선의로' 행동해도 무례하게 보인다.
❌ ① elevate — confirms — benevolently: '높이다'는 devalue의 반의어로 문맥과 반대.
❌ ② devalue — denies — benevolently: '부정하다'는 기대 확인과 반대.
❌ ④ devalue — confirms — maliciously: '악의적으로'는 benevolently와 반대.
det.tip: devalue(평가절하하다) ↔ elevate(높이다). confirm(확인하다) ↔ deny(부정하다). benevolently(선의로) ↔ maliciously(악의적으로).

questions.passage: We learn many stereotypes from the media, rather than our personal experiences. Media offerings (A)[repeatedly / rarely] present viewers with depictions of persons from all races and ethnicities, people living in poverty and older adults that leave impressions of what they are like. Too often, these depictions devalue and reduce members belonging to these groups to a simple and single concept. Then, when we interact with persons from these social categories, stereotypes are (B)[triggered / suppressed] without our even being aware of it. These stereotypes generate in us an expectation of how a member of the group will behave. When we then act on those expectations, we precipitate a self-fulfilling prophecy. We see the behavior that confirms our expectation whether or not it is actually (C)[present / absent]. Thus, if we assume that someone is rude to us, they will appear rude, even when they act benevolently.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② repeatedly — triggered — present: 미디어가 '반복적으로' 묘사를 보여주고, 고정관념이 '촉발'되며, 실제로 '존재'하든 안 하든 확인 행동을 본다.
❌ ① rarely — triggered — present: '드물게'는 반복 노출과 반대.
❌ ③ repeatedly — suppressed — present: '억제된'은 촉발과 반대.
❌ ④ repeatedly — triggered — absent: '부재하는'으로 바꾸면 맥락 훼손.
det.tip: repeatedly(반복적으로) ↔ rarely(드물게). trigger(촉발하다) ↔ suppress(억제하다). present(존재하는) ↔ absent(부재하는).

questions.passage: We learn many stereotypes from the media, rather than our (A)[personal / collective] experiences. Media offerings repeatedly present viewers with depictions of persons from all races and ethnicities, people living in poverty and older adults that leave impressions of what they are like. Too often, these depictions devalue and (B)[reduce / expand] members belonging to these groups to a simple and single concept. Then, when we interact with persons from these social categories, stereotypes are triggered without our even being aware of it. These stereotypes generate in us an expectation of how a member of the group will behave. When we then act on those expectations, we (C)[precipitate / prevent] a self-fulfilling prophecy. We see the behavior that confirms our expectation whether or not it is actually present. Thus, if we assume that someone is rude to us, they will appear rude, even when they act benevolently.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① personal — reduce — precipitate: 미디어 vs '개인적' 경험, 구성원을 단순 개념으로 '축소', 자기실현적 예언을 '촉진'한다.
❌ ② collective — reduce — precipitate: '집단적'은 원문 personal과 불일치.
❌ ③ personal — expand — precipitate: '확장하다'는 단순화와 반대.
❌ ④ personal — reduce — prevent: '방지하다'는 촉진과 반대.
det.tip: personal(개인적인) ↔ collective(집단적인). reduce(축소하다) ↔ expand(확장하다). precipitate(촉진하다) ↔ prevent(방지하다).

questions.passage: We learn many stereotypes from the media, rather than our personal experiences. Media offerings repeatedly present viewers with depictions of persons from all races and ethnicities, people living in poverty and older adults that leave ①<u>impressions</u> of what they are like. Too often, these depictions devalue and reduce members belonging to these groups to a simple and single concept. Then, when we interact with persons from these social categories, stereotypes are ②<u>triggered</u> without our even being aware of it. These stereotypes generate in us an ③<u>expectation</u> of how a member of the group will behave. When we then act on those expectations, we precipitate a self-fulfilling prophecy. We see the behavior that confirms our expectation whether or not it is actually ④<u>absent</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ absent → present: 기대를 확인하는 행동이 실제로 '존재하든' 아니든이라는 맥락입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① impressions: 어떤 사람인지에 대한 '인상'을 남긴다 — 적절.
✅ ② triggered: 고정관념이 '촉발'된다 — 적절.
✅ ③ expectation: 집단 구성원의 행동에 대한 '기대'를 생성 — 적절.
❌ ④ absent → present: '부재하든 아니든'이 아니라 '존재하든 아니든' — 부적절. ← 정답
det.tip: present(존재하는) ↔ absent(부재하는)

questions.passage: We learn many stereotypes from the media, rather than our personal experiences. Media offerings repeatedly present viewers with ①<u>depictions</u> of persons from all races and ethnicities, people living in poverty and older adults that leave impressions of what they are like. Too <u>often</u>, these depictions <u>devalue</u> and reduce members belonging to these groups to a simple and single concept. Then, when we interact with persons from these social categories, stereotypes are triggered without our even being ③<u>aware</u> of it. These stereotypes generate in us an expectation of how a member of the group will <u>behave</u>. When we then act on those expectations, we precipitate a self-fulfilling ④<u>prophecy</u>. We see the behavior that confirms our expectation whether or not it is actually present. Thus, if we assume that someone is rude to us, they will appear rude, even when they act benevolently.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② expand → reduce: 구성원을 단순한 개념으로 '축소'한다는 맥락입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① depictions: 인종과 민족의 '묘사'를 보여준다 — 적절.
❌ ② expand → reduce: '확장'이 아니라 '축소'하여 단순한 개념으로 만든다 — 부적절. ← 정답
✅ ③ aware: 인식하지 못한 채 촉발 — 적절.
✅ ④ prophecy: 자기실현적 '예언' — 적절.
det.tip: reduce(축소하다) ↔ expand(확장하다). reduce A to B: A를 B로 축소하다.

questions.passage: We learn many stereotypes from the media, rather than our personal experiences. Media offerings repeatedly present viewers with depictions of persons from all races and ethnicities, people living in poverty and older adults that leave impressions of what they are like. Too often, these depictions ①<u>devalue</u> and reduce members belonging to these groups to a simple and single concept. Then, when we interact with persons from these social categories, stereotypes are triggered without our even being aware of it. These stereotypes ②<u>generate</u> in us an expectation of how a member of the group will behave. When we then act on those expectations, we ③<u>prevent</u> a self-fulfilling prophecy. We see the behavior that confirms our expectation whether or not it is actually present. Thus, if we assume that someone is rude to us, they will appear rude, even when they act ④<u>benevolently</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ prevent → precipitate: 기대에 따라 행동하면 자기실현적 예언을 '촉진'한다는 맥락입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① devalue: 구성원을 '평가절하'한다 — 적절.
✅ ② generate: 기대를 '생성'한다 — 적절.
❌ ③ prevent → precipitate: '방지'가 아니라 '촉진/야기'한다 — 부적절. ← 정답
✅ ④ benevolently: '선의로' 행동해도 무례하게 보인다 — 적절.
det.tip: precipitate(촉진하다, 야기하다) ↔ prevent(방지하다).

Too often, these depictions devalue and reduce members belonging to these groups to a simple and single concept. Then, when we __________ with persons from these social categories, stereotypes are triggered without our even being aware of it. These stereotypes generate in us an expectation of how a member of the group will behave. When we then act on those expectations, we precipitate a self-fulfilling prophecy. We see the behavior that confirms our expectation whether or not it is actually present. Thus, if we assume that someone is rude to us, they will appear rude, even when they act benevolently.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: interact(상호작용하다): 사회적 범주의 사람들과 '상호작용'할 때 고정관념이 촉발된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ interact: 사회적 범주의 사람들과 '상호작용'할 때 고정관념이 촉발 — 적절.
❌ ① reduce: '축소하다'는 앞 문장의 행위로, 빈칸 뒤 with와 결합하면 문맥 부적절.
❌ ② present: '제시하다'는 미디어 주어의 행위로, we의 행위가 아님.
❌ ③ generate: '생성하다'는 뒤 문장의 고정관념 주어 행위로, 빈칸 문맥과 불일치.
det.tip: interact with ~: ~와 상호작용하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: precipitate(촉진하다, 야기하다): 기대에 따라 행동하면 자기실현적 예언을 '야기'한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ precipitate: 기대에 따라 행동 → 자기실현적 예언 '야기' — 적절.
❌ ① assume: '가정하다'는 뒷문장 행위로, 예언을 만드는 동사로 부적절.
❌ ② reduce: '축소하다'는 앞 문장의 행위로, 예언과 무관.
❌ ④ interact: '상호작용하다'는 앞 문장에서 이미 사용된 행위.
det.tip: precipitate = '촉진하다, 야기하다'. 화학에서 '침전시키다'의 뜻도 있음.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① devalue: reduce와 병렬. 묘사가 구성원을 '평가절하'하고 축소 — 적절.
❌ ② confirm: '확인하다'는 뒷문장의 기대 확인 맥락이지, and reduce와 병렬 불가.
❌ ③ behave: '행동하다'는 집단 구성원의 행위로, 묘사의 행위가 아님.
❌ ④ present: '제시하다'는 미디어의 행위로, 빈칸 주어 depictions과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: devalue(평가절하하다): de-(부정 접두사) + value(가치). reduce A to B: A를 B로 축소하다.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 depictions의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② portrayals: '묘사, 표현'으로 depictions과 동의어.
❌ ① statistics: '통계'는 수치 자료.
❌ ③ criticisms: '비판'은 묘사가 아님.
❌ ④ regulations: '규제'는 법적 조치.
det.tip: depiction = portrayal = representation (묘사, 표현)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 precipitate의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ bring about: '야기하다, 초래하다'로 precipitate와 동의어.
❌ ① slow down: '늦추다'는 반대 의미.
❌ ② look into: '조사하다'는 원인 규명이지 야기가 아님.
❌ ④ put off: '연기하다'는 촉진과 반대.
det.tip: precipitate = bring about = cause = trigger (야기하다, 촉진하다)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 benevolently의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: benevolently(선의로, 자비롭게): 상대가 '선의로' 행동해도 무례하게 보인다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ kindly: '친절하게'로 benevolently와 동의어.
❌ ① aggressively: '공격적으로'는 반의어.
❌ ② indifferently: '무관심하게'는 선의와 다른 뉘앙스.
❌ ③ reluctantly: '마지못해'는 의지 부족이지 선의가 아님.
det.tip: benevolently(선의로) = kindly = generously. bene-(좋은) + vol(의지) → 좋은 의지.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 present가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) present: 보여주다, 제시하다. (B) present: 존재하는, 현존하는.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 제시하다 — (B) 존재하는: (A)는 동사로 '시청자에게 묘사를 제시하다', (B)는 형용사로 '실제로 존재하는'.
❌ ① (A) 존재하는 — (B) 제시하다: (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀜.
❌ ② (A) 선물하다 — (B) 현재의: (A)는 '선물'이 아니라 '제시', (B)는 '현재'보다 '존재하는'이 정확.
❌ ④ (A) 제시하다 — (B) 현재의: (B)는 '시간상 현재'가 아니라 '존재 여부'.

다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a fixed, overly simplified idea or image of a particular type of person or thing"

det.korean: stereotype(고정관념): 특정 유형의 사람이나 사물에 대한 고정되고 지나치게 단순화된 관념.
det.analysis:
✅ ② stereotype: '고정관념'으로 정의와 정확히 일치.
❌ ① prejudice: '편견'은 부정적 선입견이나 고정된 이미지와는 다름.
❌ ③ assumption: '가정'은 증거 없는 믿음이지만 특정 유형에 국한되지 않음.
❌ ④ perspective: '관점'은 보는 시각이지 고정된 이미지가 아님.
det.tip: stereotype(고정관념) = fixed, oversimplified image. stereo-(고정된) + type(유형).

questions.passage: We learn many stereotypes from the media, rather than our personal experiences. Media offerings repeatedly present viewers with depictions of persons from all races and ethnicities, people living in poverty and older adults that leave __________ of what they are like. Too often, these depictions devalue and reduce members belonging to these groups to a simple and single concept. Then, when we interact with persons from these social categories, stereotypes are triggered without our even being aware of it. These stereotypes generate in us an expectation of how a member of the group will behave. When we then act on those expectations, we precipitate a self-fulfilling prophecy. We see the behavior that confirms our expectation whether or not it is actually present. Thus, if we assume that someone is rude to us, they will appear rude, even when they act benevolently.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ impressions: 그들이 어떤 사람인지에 대한 '인상'을 남긴다 — 적절.
❌ ① stereotypes: '고정관념'은 첫 문장 주제이나 빈칸에는 부적절.
❌ ② depictions: '묘사'는 앞에서 이미 사용된 단어로 반복.
❌ ③ categories: '범주'는 뒷문장에서 사회적 범주로 사용됨.
det.tip: leave impressions of ~: ~에 대한 인상을 남기다.
